title: Tax calculation declares whether the base includes tax
question: Separate gross-to-net extraction from net-to-gross addition; percentage units and intermediate/output rounding can change the result.

evidence.title: VAT arithmetic requires a gross/net interpretation
explanation: The VAT helpers select gross/net interpretation through an explicit argument or tag, apply multiplication/division by1+p/100, and then reconstruct Money under the library precision policy.
addVat/removeVat and getVat have distinct bases; reading the helpers confirms the tag selects a calculation branch, not jurisdiction or legally applicable rates.

Dintero Money receiver, a supplied percentage and an explicit/tagged inclusive interpretation; constructor and Big.js precision remain source-selected. At percentage-100 the gross-removal multiplier is zero; intermediate reconstruction can make add/remove noninverse. This is not a generic Rate-only tax specification. No upstream execution. Prior R1-M1 dependency contracts are reused only within their recorded bounds. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Included and excluded tax use different bases and rounding boundaries
explanation: DefaultCalculator extracts included tax as gross-gross/(1+r), but excluded tax as net*r, rounding the returned tax amount to a whole unit.

No tax eligibility, jurisdiction, currency, rate-effective-date or statutory rounding policy is established. Dintero uses percentage input and rounds a reconstructed net before rate multiplication; these formulas are not universally equivalent under finite scale.

evidence.title: Tax preserves a chosen net or gross component
explanation: flat_tax can keep gross while quantizing a reduced net or keep net while quantizing an increased gross. TaxedMoney then computes tax as gross-net and checks currency compatibility.

Reapplying flat_tax to already different net/gross components uses the current chosen component, not a universal replace-tax rule. No jurisdiction, effective-date, exemption or statutory precision is resolved.

evidence.title: Tax-inclusive example derives residual tax after subtotal truncation
explanation: The tax-inclusive example divides the total by1+taxRate, truncates subtotal to the currency unit, and assigns the remainder as total minus subtotal tax.
This is an explicit illustrative residual-ownership choice, not an independently validated legal tax algorithm or generic percentage Rate operation.

Supplied inclusive price, rate denominator nonzero and a jurisdiction that intentionally chooses this truncation/subtraction convention. Rate-1 makes the denominator zero; truncating subtotal and subtracting it can differ from independently rounding a calculated tax amount. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Invoice and cart tax declare different bases and residual rounding
explanation: The invoice example taxes subtotal after discount, whereas the cart applies a VAT allocation directly to subtotal and adds shipping; percentage ratios are native-rounded integer weights.
These are different illustrative bases and residual mechanisms. A fixed discount is not clipped to subtotal in the calculation helper.

The respective example UI and helper inputs, valid Dinero currency/scale and allocator-admissible percentage ratios. A fixed discount above subtotal makes the taxable amount negative; percentage above100 can create an invalid complementary allocation weight. These are source paths, not legal tax conclusions.
